summary: SQLx transactional outbox worker-cycle seam composing claim, dispatch, and SQL state mutation.
claim_boundary: Single-cycle worker seam only. This slice compiles an async run_sqlx_outbox_worker_cycle function that claims rows through the SQLx drain adapter, dispatches each claimed row through an injected runtime-neutral transport executor, marks successful rows published, and marks dispatch-planning/transport failures dead-letter with non-empty reasons. It does not spawn or schedule a daemon, run continuously, contact a live database in tests, publish to a live broker, call a live gRPC server, implement retry/backoff policy, or prove delivery guarantees/SLOs.

facets.F1_simplicity: The worker app is a thin composition layer over existing claim, dispatch, and mutation seams instead of introducing a scheduler, broker SDK, gRPC client, or bespoke service-specific worker code.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: The single-cycle API preserves the separable boundaries needed for future horizontally scaled workers: queue claim, dispatch execution, SQL state mutation, and per-event reporting remain independently testable and observable.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests cover Published report state validation, DeadLetter reason/state validation, mutation event-id matching, cycle count drift, event-id drift, dispatch validation errors feeding the dead-letter path, and mixed published/dead-letter cycle counts.
facets.F5_quality: Focused worker tests plus the 39-package backbone check/test/clippy/fmt matrix, cargo-deny, license-policy, cargo-prefix, catalog/data-class known-blocker probes, parse/config validation, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F7_security_privacy: The worker carries only operational outbox metadata through reports, delegates tenant-scoped SQL mutation to the SQLx drain adapter, and adds no raw message/mail/post payload content.
facets.F11_observability: OutboxWorkerCycleReport records table, tenant, worker, claimed/published/dead-letter counts, per-event transport ack metadata, mutation reports, and dead-letter reasons for future runtime telemetry correlation.
